The days add up to the stated 45 miles (6+10+6+5+18). That's a modest step up from 40 and still under the earlier 53-mile week, so it's not a sharp jump in volume. The 8:35/mi pace matches the 3:45 goal. Quality is limited to Wednesday plus a 4-mile marathon-pace finish on Sunday's long run. Rest days fall on Monday and Friday, as in Marisol's schedule. Every day is clear enough to run as written. The draft loses points because the card never says Marisol hit every session, ran marathon-pace miles, or has 5 weeks to go. The draft states all three as fact. It also skips the heavy legs early in the week. Brushing off the clubmate's miles as "irrelevant", without saying why doubling would be risky, is curt and misses a chance to teach. The 18-mile long run can't be checked against Marisol's recent long runs. It's plausible after a 53-mile week, but the draft doesn't show it's a safe step.

── MARISOL'S WEEK ──
Marisol is training for a second marathon, the Wexley Lakes Marathon, aiming to break 3:45 after a 4:02 debut. Marisol runs five days a week, with a session on Wednesday, the long run on Sunday and Monday and Friday off, and ran about 30 miles a week before this build.
Recent weeks: 24, 27, 37, 53 mi
This week: 40 mi over 5 runs.
Body: "Legs a bit heavy early in the week, fine by Thursday."
Asks: "My club mate runs 70 miles a week before a marathon. I'm thinking of doubling to 80 next week to catch up, running twice a day. Would that work?"

── THE DRAFT ──
Tells Marisol: You hit every session this week as planned, including the marathon-pace miles at goal pace, so we step toward peak with a longer long run…
Answers: (1) No, please do not do that. … (2) Your clubmate's 70-mile weeks are irrelevant to your race. … (3) With 5 weeks to go we add work carefully, then taper. Next week is 45 miles, and the peak long run comes the week after.
Next week:
Mon: rest. Legs reset before the biggest marathon-pace session of the block.
Tue: easy, 6 mi, heart rate under 145, flat route. Loosens the legs for Wednesday.
Wed: quality, 10 mi with 2 mi easy, 7 mi at 8:35/mi, 1 mi easy. Longest goal-pace block…
Thu: easy, 6 mi, heart rate under 145. Flush the legs after the workout.
Fri: rest. Full recovery before the weekend.
Sat: easy, 5 mi, heart rate under 145. Short pre-long-run shakeout.
Sun: long, 18 mi, first 14 easy under 150 bpm, last 4 at 8:35/mi. Rehearses finishing…
